repl.description: Start an interactive NestJS REPL for Meanderaw services

start.description: Run the Meanderaw application. With no arguments it sweeps every meander into output/meanders.sqlite — the whole lattice's unit space, enumerated and classified, then the historical corpus's hardcoded Codes beyond that budget; with --args="--rows <n> --columns <n> --code <code>" it writes that one row; with --check (or the `check` configuration, `nx run meanderaw:start:check`) it regenerates that same sweep into a throwaway database and fails if it disagrees with the committed one, which `guard-code` runs on every commit that affects meanderaw. `build` compiles this project rather than drawing anything, so populating the database is this target's job. The `check` and `write` configurations both run the drift check: `guard-code`'s own `--configuration` (`check` for the pre-commit gate, `write` for the auto-fix pass) forwards down to this dependency, and there is nothing here for a `write` pass to fix — the committed database is populated by a real `start` run a person chooses to make, not by an aggregator rewriting it from a branch — so `write` reruns the same read-only check rather than falling back to a bare sweep that would overwrite the committed database as a side effect. Invoking `guard-code` for this project without an explicit `--configuration` is unsupported: every caller (the pre-commit hook, the validate-code skill) always passes one, and omitting it would resolve this dependency to the bare sweep instead.
